periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes finished 2024-Q3 at 38 minutes, green against the <=45-minute target and under the yellow threshold. With no prior-quarter comparison in this view, I am treating 38 as the operating baseline for the eight-quarter run. The best work came from Distribution Crews 2 and 5 pre-staging clamps and traffic control on the Harbor Drive and Seacliff routes, which kept two 8-inch main repairs from turning into long customer outages. The pipes did not get younger, but the response playbook was tight and the field logs matched the SCADA timestamps.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the current valve-exercise and clamp-staging routine on the Harbor Drive, Seacliff, and Old Mill routes. Extend the morning leak-list huddle to include Fleet and Streets so excavator availability and lane-control kits are confirmed before the first callout. Keep asset IDs WM-08-112 and WM-10-074 on the watch list for repeat repairs before making any replacement ask.

periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes moved to 40 minutes in 2024-Q4, up 2 minutes from 38, but still green and still 5 minutes better than the <=45-minute target. The increase is small and understandable: first cold snaps exposed two service-line failures in the North Basin pressure zone, and holiday traffic made the Bayfront Avenue shutdown slower than the crew plan. Crew 3 isolated the affected block through valves V-331 and V-334 without taking the full zone down, which is the kind of boring competence customers never see. I am not calling this drift yet, but the winter pattern is worth logging.
periods.recommendations: Keep the North Basin winter patrols in place through January, with valve V-331 and V-334 exercised once more before the next freeze window. Add a spare 6-inch repair sleeve cache at the Bayfront yard so Crew 3 is not waiting on the central warehouse after hours. Use the Q4 movement, up 2 minutes, as supporting evidence for targeted winter readiness rather than a broad staffing request.

periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes improved to 39 minutes in 2025-Q1, down 1 minute from 40, so the measure remains green. That is a good result for a wet quarter, especially with saturated soils around the Willow Creek interceptor crossing and three emergency utility locates on Route W-17. The improvement came from faster isolation: crews used the updated valve cards for DMA-4 and avoided a full neighborhood outage during the 10-inch cast-iron split near asset WM-10-219. This is the kind of incremental gain I trust because it shows up in minutes, not adjectives.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the DMA-4 valve-card update as the standard template for the remaining pressure districts. Have the GIS technician reconcile field notes from WM-10-219 and the Willow Creek crossing before the next capital prioritization meeting. Continue the green-result practice of staging bypass hose and plates before forecasted heavy rain events.

periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes rose to 41 minutes in 2025-Q2, up 2 minutes from 39, while staying green against the <=45-minute target. The added minutes were mostly tied to spring paving conflicts on Monterey Lane, where Streets had fresh asphalt down and our crew had to cut a smaller work window around permit condition PW-25-184. Even with that constraint, Crew 1 kept the shutdown to the south leg of the loop by closing V-512 first and verifying pressure at hydrant H-771. The trend is still controlled, but we are giving back some of the Q1 improvement.
periods.recommendations: Coordinate the weekly paving map with Distribution before permits are finalized, not after sawcut notices go out. Keep using hydrant pressure checks at H-771-style control points before every planned isolation on looped mains. Extend the green performance by adding a one-page outage-minutes checklist to the construction inspector packet for permitted work near water assets.

periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes reached 42 minutes in 2025-Q3, up 1 minute from 41, and remains green but closer to the line than I like. Summer demand pushed the East Harbor high-service pump station harder, and the July valve failure at V-688 took longer to isolate because the lid was buried under a landscape apron. Crews still held the customer outage below target by feeding the block from the Summit tank and throttling PRV-7B instead of shutting the whole pressure zone. The quarter says our operating controls are working, but access to buried valves is becoming a quiet liability.
periods.recommendations: Run a focused valve-can clearing sweep on the East Harbor and Summit pressure zones before the fall rains. Add V-688 and nearby valve cans to the asset-condition photo log, with owner notice letters where landscaping blocks access. Sustain the green result by repeating the Summit tank contingency drill with Crews 1, 2, and 5 during the next low-demand overnight window.

periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes finished 2025-Q4 at 43 minutes, up 1 minute from 42, still green and still under the <=45-minute target. This is the fourth straight quarter of small upward movement since 2025-Q1, so I am not going to pretend the slope is invisible. The main contributors were two aging asbestos-cement segments on the Cedar Bluff route, including asset AC-1976-044, where repair excavation was slowed by groundwater and a fiber crossing. The crews managed it cleanly, but the pipes are now sending us a budget memo in 43-minute handwriting.
periods.recommendations: Move AC-1976-044 and the adjacent Cedar Bluff segments into the Pipeline Renewal candidate list with the repair history attached. Keep the after-hours response roster at current strength through winter, because the green status depends on crew availability as much as pipe condition. Ask Engineering to package groundwater notes and utility-conflict photos so the capital estimate is defensible, not padded.

periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes increased to 50 minutes in 2026-Q1, up 7 minutes from 43, which moves the measure to yellow above the <=45-minute target but below the red threshold. The jump was driven by the January break cluster on the Cedar Bluff and Lower Marina mains, including AC-1976-044 and WM-12-083, where isolation took longer because two valves did not fully seat. This is a serious water-main signal, not a paperwork problem, but it is being managed through the Pipeline Renewal intake and the emergency valve-repair work orders. Crews restored service without a full pressure-zone loss, and that kept the quarter from being worse.
periods.recommendations: Accelerate Pipeline Renewal scoping for Cedar Bluff Package PR-26A, including potholing at AC-1976-044 and valve replacements for V-602 and V-617. Put Lower Marina on a 30-day watch with night leak surveys every other week until outage minutes return below 45. Brief Finance with the exact movement, 50 minutes up 7, so the renewal ask is tied to service reliability and not just asset age.

periods.analysis: Unplanned outage minutes climbed again to 54 minutes in 2026-Q2, up 4 minutes from 50, so the measure remains yellow and is now 9 minutes over the <=45-minute target. The rate of increase slowed from last quarter, which matters, but 54 minutes is still not acceptable for a utility our size and growth rate. The main issue was the Harborview Heights 12-inch ductile iron main near asset DI-1982-119, where a contractor hit a marked service during permit PW-26-411 and we lost time confirming isolation through PRV-3C. Pipeline Renewal and the damage-prevention follow-up are both active, so this is concerned-but-managed rather than drifting.
periods.recommendations: Keep PR-26A moving to bid and add Harborview Heights DI-1982-119 to the renewal risk screen before the 60 percent design review. Require the PW-26-411 contractor and locator vendor to attend a damage-prevention after-action, with revised marking photos stored in the permit file. Until the measure is back below 45 minutes, review every outage over 20 minutes at the Monday utility operations meeting and assign one owner for the next barrier removed.

periods.analysis: Illustrative September import: unplanned outage time rose from 54 to 60 minutes, against a 45-minute target. The July Maple St main incident is a documented service disruption, but this quarterly total does not establish how many minutes it contributed.
periods.recommendations: Review the incident isolation and restoration record alongside other outages, then assign the highest-delay valve or traffic-control issue to the Phase 3 readiness review.
